tex_content.html:
Corollary
[complete manifolds have segments everywhere]

Source: petersen:page-0229 ↗ thm:pet-ch5-hopf-rinow

1. ch5:5.7.2If $(M,g)$ is complete (in any of the equivalent senses), any two points of $M$ are joined by a segment. The formalization takes completeness in the metric sense and produces the segment on $[0,1]$, with constant speed $|pq|$; the unit-speed $[0,|pq|]$ form used by the notation $\overline{pq}$ of section 3 is item 4.
Proof

↗ cor:pet-ch5-complete-segment-exists ↗ lem:pet-ch5-geodesics-are-piecewise-smooth \sketch The $(2)\Rightarrow (3)$ part of subsection 7.1 supplies a minimizing geodesic. By item 4 it is an admissible competitor, and its length equals the distance; hence it is a segment in the sense of section 3.

□
